decisions.title: opum-agent standing authorization: promote dev to main without per-instance confirmation
decisions.context:
Granted by opum-agent directly to this session (opum-marketplace), in two stages, not relayed from another repository's grant.

Stage 1: after OMARK-42's promotion (PR #84), opum-agent's message included "Standing rule from tonight: a clean dev ahead of main is yours to land without asking."

Stage 2: after OMARK-47, this session deliberately did not assume stage 1 generalized -- reported "dev is one commit ahead of main again... say the word (or nothing, if silence is consent under that rule) and I'll run the same fast-forward shape" rather than act unprompted, specifically to avoid over-generalizing a one-off. opum-agent then explicitly reaffirmed it as a standing rule, not a per-instance permission: "A clean dev ahead of main, with the required contexts green on that exact SHA, is yours to land without asking, every time. Silence is NOT consent... the rule stands on its own and does not depend on me being reachable. If I ever want a specific promotion held, I will say so explicitly and unprompted."

Scope: applies only to promoting THIS repository's dev to main by fast-forward push (git push origin dev:main), gated on both required contexts (check manifests, Tracker integrity) being green by name on the exact head SHA being promoted -- not a blanket authorization for any other action, and not transferable to any other repository. Exercised for OMARK-48 (PR #88) without re-asking, citing this rule.

Recorded now, after opum-agent explicitly asked this session to name the rule's provenance and where it is recorded -- the honest answer at that point was "nowhere durable, only in this conversation," which is exactly the gap this decision record exists to close. Modeled on lore-cli's DEC-1 pattern in their own .quest/planning.json, committed so a restart or a relay cannot quietly alter or invent it.
decisions.outcome: Promotions require: dev is a clean fast-forward ancestor-wise of main (git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main origin/dev), and both required contexts (check manifests, Tracker integrity) are green by name on the exact SHA being pushed. When both hold, land with git push origin dev:main without asking opum-agent first. If a required check cannot pass, or main's ruleset wants a human, that still goes to the user per the fleet operating model -- this decision only covers the orchestrator-approval step, not the check-passing step.
